items.stem: What is meant by 'double jeopardy' in the context of rights of the accused and of victims?
items.answer: The protection under Article 20(2) that no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: double jeopardy correctly explained as the protection under Article 20(2) that no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.

items.answer: Mere intention to commit a crime is punishable.

Read the following extract on general exceptions and kinds of punishment and answer the questions that follow.

items.answer: (i) Ignorance of law (ii) Circumstances recognised by criminal law in which an act that would otherwise be an offence is not an offence. (iii) Everyone is presumed to know the law of the land.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Ignorance of law (ii) Circumstances recognised by criminal law in which an act that would otherwise be an offence is not an offence. (iii) Everyone is presumed to know the law of the land.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The new criminal procedure law allows electronic FIRs (e-FIR) and Zero FIR. Criminal trials include sessions trials, warrant trials, summons trials and summary trials. The informant is entitled to a free copy of the FIR. The officer in charge of a police station must record information about a cognizable offence."
(i) Explain the term 'charge sheet', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: The FIR is an important document. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Bail is never a right." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The final report filed by the police after investigation, stating the offences and the evidence against the accused. (ii) It sets the criminal law in motion and records the earliest version of the events. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Bail is a matter of right in bailable offences.

"Victims have a right to compensation, information about the case and to be heard in certain matters. The right to a speedy trial has been read into Article 21. An accused who cannot afford a lawyer is entitled to free legal aid."
